steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: A sample with a library size several times below the median must not be deleted silently. steps.name: Gene-level DESeq2 Wald test, UC inflamed vs control

steps.context: Same 12000 x 12 Salmon count matrix. steps.name: GSVA hallmark scores per sample, heatmap and limma test
caveats: GSVA scores are relative within this cohort: they depend on the sample set and are not comparable to scores computed on another dataset. Say so in the output.
A hallmark that separates the groups on the heatmap is evidence of coordinated expression, not of pathway flux or activation.

Hallmark sets overlap — the inflammatory sets (TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB, INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE, INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE, IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING) share many genes, so several significant hits driven by the same genes are one finding, not four. Note the overlap before listing counts.
sample_01's ~4x lower depth adds noise to its per-gene ranks and therefore to its GSVA scores; check whether it is an outlier column in the heatmap before interpreting.
steps.context: This is the step the research question asks for. steps.name: fgsea preranked hallmark test on the Wald statistic
caveats: Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene list here; if fewer than about 50 genes pass padj < 0.05 an ORA has no power, and the ranked test on the full list is the method regardless.

steps.context: The per-sample GSVA/limma result is the primary answer, but enrichment results are method-dependent, so a second, differently-constructed test on the same contrast is the check on it. Input: the full tested-gene table from T1S2 ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, and the same human hallmark collection T2S1 used.
steps.question: Do the hallmark pathways that separate the groups in the per-sample GSVA scores also come out of a ranked group-comparison test on the same data?

grounding.reason: Ranked test on the full tested list is the default enrichment method per R-0107@976c; the disputed ranking statistic of R-0108@409f is settled in favour of the Wald statistic, stated here per R-0099@0a77.

constraints: enrichment: rank_metric = stat, the DESeq2 Wald statistic (doi:10.1101/060012; R-0099@0a77)

enrichment: gsea_input = full_ranked_list — never a thresholded gene list (doi:10.1073/pnas.0506580102)
enrichment: min_size = 15, max_size = 500 after intersection with the tested genes
enrichment: collapse_redundant = true before reporting a count of findings
Use the same human hallmark collection and version as T2S1
Set and record a random seed — permutation p-values do not reproduce without it
steps.description: Rank every tested gene by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column) — the ranking-metric dispute is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its standard error and does not saturate into ties the way a signed p-value does. acceptance_criteria: fgsea results table over the hallmark sets: NES, p, BH-adjusted p, set size after intersection with the tested genes
Leading-edge gene list for every set significant at BH < 0.05, each gene with its Wald statistic, and an explicit note of leading-edge overlap between reported sets
A concordance table naming hallmarks significant in GSVA/limma only, fgsea only, and both
The ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic) and the random seed stated in the output

caveats: The gene-level DE result is supporting material here, not the answer — do not let it displace the per-sample score deliverable the user asked for.

steps.context: Assembles T1S1 (QC and sample_01 disposition), T1S2 (gene-level fit) and T2S1/T2S2 (per-sample hallmark scores, heatmap, limma test and the ranked cross-check) into one document. plan.title: UC inflamed vs control: hallmark GSVA sample scores
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is a per-sample pathway activity readout: a score per sample for every hallmark set, a heatmap across the 12 colon samples, and an explicit statement of which hallmark pathways separate ulcerative-colitis-inflamed from control. The inputs are a 12000 x 13 raw integer count matrix from Salmon (gene symbol in column 1, one column per sample) and a 12 x 2 sample table with a condition column, 6 inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch.

The knowledge service (snapshot sha256:ad61b0ba...) returns GSVA-then-limma as the applicable procedure for a per-sample score question at 6 per group (R-0102@c84c), with MSigDB Hallmark as the first collection for human (R-0048@500d). The staged hallmark GMT is human, 50 sets, HGNC symbols — the same identifier space as the count matrix's first column, so no ID mapping is required for the GSVA step and none is planned.

Order: T1S1 does the sample-structure QC that the procedure puts before any model — blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes and detected genes per sample. sample_01 sits about 4x below the median library size; per R-0008@440d it is kept, inspected and reported, not dropped by default, and the VST/size factors down-weight it. T1S2 runs the gene-level DESeq2 Wald fit (minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios, apeglm shrinkage, BH at alpha 0.05) — this is not the answer to the question but it supplies the two things the pathway steps need: the tested-gene universe and the Wald statistic used as the fgsea ranking metric. T2S1 is the step the question asks for: GSVA on the blind-VST matrix with the Gaussian kernel (log-scale input, per R-0102), restricted to the tested genes, sets kept at 15-500 members after intersection, giving a 50 x 12 score matrix, a clustered heatmap annotated by condition, and a limma moderated t-test of each hallmark score between UC_inflamed and control with BH adjustment. T2S2 is the confirmatory ranked test — fgsea on the full tested list ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed ranking choice of R-0108 is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate) — so that the per-sample scores are not the only evidence for a pathway call. T1S3 assembles both with the reproducibility record.

The honest limits, to be stated in the report rather than discovered later: 6 vs 6 is adequate for hallmark-level signal but not for confident ranking among correlated inflammatory sets; GSVA scores are relative within this cohort and are not comparable to another dataset; a hallmark that separates the groups on the heatmap is a hypothesis about coordinated expression, not evidence of pathway flux; and enrichment results are method-dependent, so the GSVA/limma and fgsea calls are compared and their disagreement reported.

~condition with control as explicit reference level; contrast condition UC_inflamed vs control

fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark

Draw a clustered heatmap of the scores with samples in columns annotated by condition, rows z-scored for display, and a second version with rows ordered by the limma t-statistic so the separating pathways sit at the top. Then fit limma on the score matrix with the same design (~condition, control as reference), moderated t-test for UC-inflamed vs control, BH adjustment, and report a table of hallmark, mean score per group, difference, t, p and adjusted p. Report the per-sample scores for sample_01 alongside the others so any low-depth distortion is visible.
acceptance_criteria: Pathway-by-sample GSVA score matrix (retained hallmark sets x 12 samples) written to CSV
Clustered heatmap of hallmark scores across all 12 samples with a condition annotation bar, plus a version ordered by the limma statistic
limma results table for every retained hallmark: group means, difference, moderated t, raw p and BH-adjusted p, sorted by adjusted p
Explicit named list of the hallmark sets that separate UC-inflamed from control at BH < 0.05, or an explicit statement that none reach it
Number of hallmark sets retained after the 15-500 size window and the fraction of hallmark member genes found in the tested matrix
Kernel choice (Gaussian, log-scale input) and the hallmark collection version stated in the output
If the human hallmark gene sets cannot be resolved in the environment, stop and report that rather than substituting another collection — the question names hallmark activity specifically
constraints: enrichment: pathway_scores = gsva_then_limma (doi:10.1186/1471-2105-14-7)
enrichment: gene_set_collection = msigdb_hallmark_human (doi:10.1016/j.cels.2015.12.004)
enrichment: min_size = 15, max_size = 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes (doi:10.1073/pnas.0506580102)
enrichment: universe = tested_genes (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009935)
Use the Gaussian kernel because the input is log-scale VST, not integer counts (R-0102@c84c)
Use the same design as the gene-level model: ~condition with control as reference
Resolve the hallmark gene sets by what the data IS — human hallmark sets keyed on gene symbols — against whatever the environment provides; do not hard-code a path
Report the collection version alongside the results
caveats: GSVA scores are relative within this cohort: they depend on the sample set and are not comparable to scores computed on another dataset. Say so in the output.
A hallmark that separates the groups on the heatmap is evidence of coordinated expression, not of pathway flux or activation.

Hallmark sets overlap — the inflammatory sets (TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB, INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE, INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE, IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING) share many genes, so several significant hits driven by the same genes are one finding, not four. Note the overlap before listing counts.
sample_01's ~4x lower depth adds noise to its per-gene ranks and therefore to its GSVA scores; check whether it is an outlier column in the heatmap before interpreting.

grounding.reason: Question needs a score per sample at 6 per group: GSVA then limma on the scores per R-0102@c84c, human hallmark first per R-0048@500d, 15-500 size window per R-0047@fd9d.

steps.name: fgsea preranked hallmark test on the Wald statistic
steps.question: Do the hallmark pathways that separate the groups in the per-sample GSVA scores also come out of a ranked group-comparison test on the same data?
steps.context: The per-sample GSVA/limma result is the primary answer, but enrichment results are method-dependent, so a second, differently-constructed test on the same contrast is the check on it. Input: the full tested-gene table from T1S2 ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, and the same human hallmark collection T2S1 used.
steps.description: Rank every tested gene by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column) — the ranking-metric dispute is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its standard error and does not saturate into ties the way a signed p-value does. Run fgsea against the human hallmark sets with the same 15-500 size window and a fixed random seed, BH adjustment. Report NES, p, padj and the leading-edge genes of each significant set with each member's gene-level statistic, and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. Then compare directly against T2S1: a table of hallmarks called by GSVA/limma only, by fgsea only, and by both, treating the intersection as the confident set.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea results table over the hallmark sets: NES, p, BH-adjusted p, set size after intersection with the tested genes
Leading-edge gene list for every set significant at BH < 0.05, each gene with its Wald statistic, and an explicit note of leading-edge overlap between reported sets
A concordance table naming hallmarks significant in GSVA/limma only, fgsea only, and both
The ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic) and the random seed stated in the output
constraints: enrichment: rank_metric = stat, the DESeq2 Wald statistic (doi:10.1101/060012; R-0099@0a77)
enrichment: rank_metric_not = unshrunken log2 fold change alone, signed p-value with ties (doi:10.1186/s12859-017-1674-0)
enrichment: gsea_input = full_ranked_list — never a thresholded gene list (doi:10.1073/pnas.0506580102)
enrichment: min_size = 15, max_size = 500 after intersection with the tested genes
enrichment: collapse_redundant = true before reporting a count of findings
Use the same human hallmark collection and version as T2S1
Set and record a random seed — permutation p-values do not reproduce without it
caveats: Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene list here; if fewer than about 50 genes pass padj < 0.05 an ORA has no power, and the ranked test on the full list is the method regardless.

GSVA/limma and fgsea ask different questions — one tests a per-sample score, the other tests rank concentration in a group contrast — so partial disagreement is expected and is information, not an error to be resolved by picking the friendlier result.

grounding.reason: Ranked test on the full tested list is the default enrichment method per R-0107@976c; the disputed ranking statistic of R-0108@409f is settled in favour of the Wald statistic, stated here per R-0099@0a77.

steps.name: Consolidated report and reproducibility record
steps.question: Which hallmark pathways separate UC-inflamed from control colon in these 12 samples, on what evidence, and with what limits?
steps.context: Assembles T1S1 (QC and sample_01 disposition), T1S2 (gene-level fit) and T2S1/T2S2 (per-sample hallmark scores, heatmap, limma test and the ranked cross-check) into one document. The deliverables the user asked for are the per-sample pathway score table and the hallmark heatmap; those lead.
steps.description: Write the report with the per-sample hallmark score matrix and the annotated heatmap first, then the list of hallmarks separating UC-inflamed from control with their limma statistics and the fgsea concordance. Follow with the gene-level fit: design formula, reference level, contrast, thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering, number significant at padj < 0.05, MA and dispersion plots, and a gene table carrying unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold change with lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value. State the sample_01 decision and its stated reason. Close with the limits and the reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: Per-sample hallmark score table and the condition-annotated heatmap presented first, with the separating pathways named
Gene set collection name, version, ranking metric, universe (tested genes) and the 15-500 size window all stated
Design formula, reference level (control), contrast direction, alpha, n tested and n significant all stated
Gene table with log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value
Leading-edge genes per significant set carried through from T2S2

An explicit limits paragraph: 6 vs 6 is adequate for hallmark-level signal but not for confident ranking among correlated inflammatory sets; GSVA scores are cohort-relative; coordinated expression is not pathway flux; enrichment results are method-dependent and the two methods' disagreement is reported rather than reconciled
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, random seed, hallmark collection version
constraints: report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
report: effect_columns = log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange, lfcSE; rank_genes_by = shrunken_log2FoldChange (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty895)
report: fit_diagnostics = ma_plot, dispersion_plot (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#ma-plot)
report: leading_edge = per_significant_set (doi:10.1073/pnas.0506580102)
report: enrichment_report = database, version, rank_metric, universe, size_window (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009935)
report: enrichment_caveat = method_dependence (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz158)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
Do not present a hallmark hit as a mechanistic conclusion; present it as a hypothesis for follow-up
If no hallmark reaches BH < 0.05, say so plainly and report the ranking rather than lowering the threshold to produce a list
caveats: The gene-level DE result is supporting material here, not the answer — do not let it displace the per-sample score deliverable the user asked for.
Reporting a count of significant hallmark sets without collapsing the overlapping inflammatory sets overstates the number of independent findings.

grounding.reason: Report content follows the procedure's report step: shrunken and unshrunken effects (R-0085@c24d), fit diagnostics (R-0087@c53d), enrichment provenance (R-0051@01ca), leading edge (R-0105@c4a8) and the reproducibility record (R-0086@becf). R-0042 (two-method DE overlap) is not planned — only DESeq2 is run at the gene level, since the gene-level fit is supporting material rather than the deliverable.
